example: The woman at the front desk gave us directions.
rrgm_bridge: Woman names an adult female person, the counterpart to man.

domain_entries.REL: Social roles and expectations attached to women vary across cultures and have changed greatly over time; many have been challenged and revised.
domain_entries.LIN: Plural "women"; once also used in compounds where neutral terms are now common.

count_condition: An adult person who is female, or who identifies as a woman.
transfer_boundary: The roles expected of women come from culture, not from the word. Generalisations about "women" describe tendencies at most, not any individual.

common_meaning: A period of seven days; also the working days of that period.
example: I'll see you next week; she works a four-day week.
rrgm_bridge: A week is a human-made cycle of seven days, a rhythm laid over time by convention.
invariant_mi: A unit of seven consecutive days.

domain_entries.ECO: The working week sets the pattern of labour and rest.
domain_entries.REL: Weekly rhythms (market days, rest days, worship) organise community life.

count_condition: A period of seven days, or the working portion of it.
transfer_boundary: Unlike the day or year, the week matches no astronomical cycle; it is a social convention.

common_meaning: The direction toward the setting sun, opposite east; also the western part of a place, or (as "the West") Europe and North America.
example: The sun sets in the west.
rrgm_bridge: West is the direction of sunset, and also a name a group of countries gives itself.
invariant_mi: The direction opposite east, or a region lying that way.

domain_entries.PHY: Cardinal direction, where the sun sets.
domain_entries.REL: "The West" is a cultural and political grouping, not a fixed place; its boundaries are disputed.

count_condition: A direction or a region oriented westward, or the grouping called the West.
transfer_boundary: "The West" is defined by politics and history more than geography. Directions are relative: every place is west of somewhere.

common_meaning: A married woman considered in relation to her spouse.
rrgm_bridge: Wife names a role within a marriage, one end of a partnered bond.
invariant_mi: A woman in relation to the person she is married to.

domain_entries.REL: Marriage roles and expectations vary across cultures and have changed over time; legal rights of wives have expanded greatly.

count_condition: A married woman, named in relation to her spouse.
transfer_boundary: The role does not define the whole person; the expectations attached to it come from culture and law.

common_meaning: Anything or everything that; no matter what; also (informally) an expression of indifference.
example: Take whatever you need; whatever happens, call me.
rrgm_bridge: Whatever leaves the content open: any value will do.
invariant_mi: Any or every thing, with the choice left open.

domain_entries.LIN: Free relative and concessive; as a reply, can signal dismissal.

count_condition: An open choice, or indifference to the options.
transfer_boundary: As a reply, "whatever" can close a conversation without agreeing to anything.
